memory_update.text: AXTI should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a direct InP/GaAs substrate candidate, but its survival depends on evidence of InP revenue mix, capacity, customer qualification, and export-control risk.

AIIXY/AIXTRON is the cleanest tool-layer candidate for the node because it links AI optical demand to G10-AsP MOCVD orders and optoelectronics backlog, but ADR liquidity and European listing structure should be flagged.

TSEM deserves inclusion despite larger market cap because silicon-photonics customer contracts, prepayments, and NVIDIA-linked 1.6T module work create unusually direct exposure to AI optical-connectivity capacity.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed micro/small-cap speculative photonics names such as optical-engine developers and transceiver suppliers; many may fail liquidity, revenue-quality, or customer-validation screens.

node: Optical connectivity, lasers, compound-semiconductor epitaxy, and epitaxy equipment
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a small set of US-listed or US-traded public assets tied to the upstream AI optical-connectivity stack. The cleanest underfollowed chokepoint candidates are AXT for InP/GaAs substrates and AIXTRON ADR for MOCVD epitaxy tools. Tower Semiconductor is a larger but unusually pure silicon-photonics foundry read-through with recent customer-contract evidence. Lumentum is included as a high-attention reference anchor because its InP lasers and AI data-center optical products validate demand upstream into substrates and epitaxy tools. No trading recommendation is implied.
